assetRisk.scenario: Underground storage tank leak or pipework failure causing subsurface aquifer contamination
assetRisk.source: ~37,000 retail fuel stations across the national downstream marketing network, housing ~110,000 underground storage tanks (USTs) and associated pressurized product pipework. Baseline failure frequency of 0.0004 incidents per station-year reflects ~1 significant subsurface hydrocarbon release penetrating the water table per 2,500 station-years (~14.8 events/yr across the estate), grounded in international UST release statistics (EPA 40 CFR Part 280 release reporting trends and CONCAWE retail environmental studies) and national statutory environmental audit data. Consequence of INR 6 Cr (~$720,000) reflects multi-well monitoring and plume delineation, hazardous soil excavation and off-site bio-remediation, long-term groundwater pump-and-treat / air sparging operations (typically 18-36 months), tank/pipework decommissioning and forecourt civil reconstruction, lost dealer throughput during prolonged excavation, and statutory environmental compensation penalties levied by environmental tribunals and state pollution control boards (e.g., CPCB/NGT guidelines for groundwater restitution). Alpha (0.35) reflects the causal share attributable to information, detection, and surveillance lag (e.g., slow 0.2 gal/hr pinhole leaks or line weeping masked beneath diurnal thermal expansion cycles, water ingress ignored due to faulty water-paste dips, and un-reconciled book-to-physical inventory variances under API RP 1621). Beta (0.40) reflects the 7-agent squad's efficacy in autonomous continuous temperature-compensated Statistical Inventory Reconciliation (SIR, Agent 1), automated meter drift isolation (Agent 4), and proactive mobile HSSE containment sump inspection auditing (Agent 3).

rationale: P53 Retail Territory Manager oversees operational governance, statutory safety compliance, wetstock inventory integrity, and dealer commercial performance across an assigned geographic territory of retail fuel stations. Sizing at 900 seats represents ~2.9% of total enterprise headcount (~31,000 staff), sized across ~37,000 retail stations at an average span of ~40-42 stations per territory manager (distributed across ~75-80 divisional sales offices with 11-12 territory managers per division, managing a blended network of company-owned dealer-operated CODO, dealer-owned dealer-operated DODO, and company-operated COCO outlets). Asset Capital is strictly null in accordance with value_model.js rules: retail territory managers are mobile field auditors and franchise commercial managers who do not sit on the critical path of physical asset operations; fuel dispensing and forecourt operations proceed continuously 24/7 without gating by territory manager visits, preserving the 'load-bearing zero' discipline observed in P19 (Process Safety), P27 (Pipeline Integrity), P30 (Inspection), and P48 (Hydrocarbon Accounting). Furthermore, >90% of retail stations are dealer-operated where commercial meter giveaway and local stock variances are absorbed at the dealership level rather than on the refiner-marketer balance sheet, and secondary distribution bridging is owned upstream by P49 Distribution Planner. Asset Risk models major underground storage tank leaks and pipework failures causing subsurface aquifer contamination across 37,000 stations at INR 6 Cr consequence with alpha*beta held to 0.14 (avoiding INR 1.24 Cr/yr in expected environmental and statutory losses). Resource Recovery is strictly null as downstream retail marketing operates far beyond the subsurface extraction boundary and portfolio rules prohibit joint Integrity and Recovery claims.
caveats: 1. Asset capital is maintained as strictly null to protect the model's 'load-bearing zero' discipline; if an operator insists on capturing commercial dispenser calibration giveaway on its company-owned company-operated (COCO) retail network (~2,500 COCO stations retailing ~25 Mbbl/yr of motor fuels, where 0.02% over-dispensing giveaway is recovered via Agent 4 at INR 350/bbl retail margin), that volume mechanism would generate ~INR 1.75 Cr/yr, but is excluded here to avoid conflating dealer-absorbed margins with enterprise asset capital. 2. Secondary delivery replenishment and stockout prevention (Agent 2) are governed upstream by P49 Distribution Planner; claiming retail station dry-out hours in P53 would double-count against P49's secondary distribution balancing. 3. Consequence of INR 6 Cr assumes moderate-to-severe plume migration impacting local drinking water aquifers; soil-only excavation confined within tank sumps typically resolves under INR 50-80 Lakhs, whereas multi-acre off-site plume contamination can exceed INR 15 Cr in statutory compensation.
